cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Make It Their Idea
cards.instruction: Make an unwanted task sound appealing enough that someone volunteers for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. These eighty wedding place cards need names. Your bin labels have better lettering than our invitations.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like calligraphy. I hate copying guest lists.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. I'd read the names. You'd only do the beautiful part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your aunt will complain if I use purple.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle my aunt. The ink colour could be entirely yours.

mechanism: Praise a former pupil's lettering as ready for a real commission, removing the unwanted copying and family criticism so B is tempted to volunteer.
confusable: Not issuing homework: A must make the unattractive task appealing enough for B to choose it, using claimed training and qualified praise as the sales method.
comparison: Artistic control over wedding cards differs from control over a shed and its rules.
seedUse: Retains eighty place cards/bin labels/purple/aunt; makes A's supposed teaching determine offered status and protection.
